title: Legaltech Rundown: Goodwin Expands Partnership With Microsoft, Thomson Reuters Rolls Out Cocounsel Legal Globally, and More
source_used: Thomson Reuters press release (PR Newswire via Yahoo Finance Canada, 14 Oct 2026) for the CoCounsel half; Law.com body unreadable (sign-in wall); Goodwin half from headlines only
key_facts: Law.com's Legaltech Rundown (16 Oct 2026) is a weekly update of legal technology happenings; its headline names Goodwin's expanded partnership with Microsoft and Thomson Reuters's global rollout of CoCounsel Legal.
Thomson Reuters said on 14 Oct 2026 that it is making the next generation of CoCounsel Legal available globally and adding a Multinational Profile.
The Multinational Profile brings legal content from more than 100 countries and territories into a single CoCounsel Legal workflow for cross-border research.
The upgraded platform will be available to customers in more than 90 countries and territories throughout 2026; Australia, Canada and the UK will soon have access.
David Wong, Chief Product Officer of Thomson Reuters, said research tools 'stop at the border' and that the Multinational Profile changes that.

Capabilities listed: research reports using Westlaw and Practical Law content, matter workspaces, tabular analysis of documents in bulk, and integrations; not every capability is available in every geography.
Law360 headline of 14 Oct 2026: 'Goodwin Expands Microsoft Partnership For Its Proprietary AI' (no text readable).
quote_evidence: Thomson Reuters is solving that with the new Multinational Profile, a capability that brings legal content from more than 100 countries and territories into a single CoCounsel Legal workflow.
Not every capability is available in every geography, and availability will continue to expand.
The Legaltech Rundown is a weekly update of legal tech happenings that might have gone under the radar.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading legal-information company says its AI assistant now covers cross-border research, on its own claims.
event_date: 14 Oct 2026 (Thomson Reuters announcement; Law360 Goodwin report); Law.com rundown 16 Oct 2026
notes: Paywalled roundup; a paid press release stands in for the Thomson Reuters half; Goodwin half unverified beyond the headline.
